title: Mexico opens bidding for 52 passenger trains on the Mexico City–Nuevo Laredo corridor
excerpt: Mexico's rail agency launched an international bid for 52 passenger trains for the Mexico City–Nuevo Laredo and Mexico City–Guadalajara corridors, with the award set for January 8, 2027.
content:
Mexico is moving ahead with its plan to bring passenger trains back to the border. The federal government has launched an international bidding process to buy 52 new passenger trains for the Mexico City–Nuevo Laredo and Mexico City–Guadalajara corridors, according to Industry & Energy Magazine.

The purchase is being run by the Agencia de Trenes y Transporte Público Integrado (ATTRAPI), headed by Andrés Lajous, under the new law for strategic infrastructure investment. The call for bids covers 27 long-distance trains and 25 short-distance trains, through an open electronic international tender.

Unlike past rail purchases, which were paid for with budget funds, this one may use public, private or mixed financing, and the winning supplier could securitize collection rights through a trust. The winner will not only supply the trains but also handle their commissioning, maintenance and the equipping of related workshops. The agency plans a 20 percent advance per fiscal year, with VAT included, and a contract running through December 31, 2034.

The calendar is already moving: bidding documents were available until Tuesday, November 10, for one peso; the first clarification meeting is set for Thursday, November 12, 2026, and the award is scheduled for January 8, 2027, though dates could shift given the technical and financial complexity. No total price for the 52 trains has been confirmed.

The purchase fits into a broader expansion: ATTRAPI's 2026–2030 program includes 13 rail route construction projects and a goal of more than 3,000 kilometers of passenger lines. For comparison, the agency's predecessor bought 47 and 15 passenger trains in 2025 for about 26,000 million pesos. But buying the trains does not mean service starts right away — the routes still depend on finishing construction, rail systems and safety testing before passengers can board.

Source: Industry & Energy Magazine (energymagazine.mx).

Update — November 12, 2026

More details of the tender have now been published. The trains will be diesel-electric, and the tender — number FL-09-JZO-009JZO001-I-1-2026 — covers the second phase of the Querétaro–Saltillo project, according to Info-Transportes. The full calendar is now set: the first clarification meeting takes place today, Thursday, November 12, with a second on November 20; manufacturers and suppliers must submit their bids by December 18, 2026; the award is scheduled for January 8, 2027, at 5:30 p.m., and the contract signing for January 21, 2027. The contract covers maintenance and workshop equipment through December 31, 2034. No total cost for the 52 trains has been confirmed.

Separately, President Claudia Sheinbaum said on November 5 that the government plans to invest about 700 billion pesos to build roughly 2,500 kilometers of passenger rail during her term, and that the Mexico City–Querétaro line is about 32 percent complete, with about 18,500 workers on 12 construction fronts.

Sources: Transporte.mx, November 9, 2026; Info-Transportes, November 11, 2026; La Elección, November 5, 2026.
